info.title: OpenPinsheet API
info.description: OpenPinsheet publishes where the pin was, by date and hole, as open data under the Open Database License 1.0. GET /live and GET /pins need a reader key: a reader logs in with GitHub at GET /auth/github and gets one, shown once. A data partner delivers the pins of one ground for one day with POST /submissions, using a partner key from the account page at /v1/account. Both keys go as Authorization: Bearer. Once a day is closed it is frozen into files served under https://data.openpinsheet.com/v1, without a key. Errors are problem details (RFC 9457) with a fixed code in error. Every other path answers 404 not_found, a wrong method 405 method_not_allowed with Allow, and an unexpected failure 500 internal_error. HEAD works wherever GET does and is counted like it. The account page and the review links under /v1/account and /v1/review are pages for people and not described here. A change a client would misread comes as /v2, run next to /v1 for a year.

externalDocs.description: Source code of this API (AGPL-3.0-or-later) and the data format; this description is Apache-2.0

get.description: A reader key is required, as Authorization: Bearer. A reader logs in with GitHub at GET /auth/github and gets a key, shown once; one key per GitHub account is active and a new login replaces the old one. Any website may call it (CORS '*'), and a script may read the limit headers. Limits per GitHub account, kept across a new login: 30 requests a minute and 1000 per UTC day; a key bound to a website's origins may have another day limit and counts its minute limit per visitor, with a ceiling of about 300 a minute for the key (Cloudflare counts per location). Every answer that spends a request carries X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset; a malformed box is refused before anything is counted. For files on data.openpinsheet.com no key is needed. The answer is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection like a published file, with the columns of FORMAT.md 2 and today's UTC date as as_of. The box is at most 0.5 degrees wide and 0.5 degrees high; a box cannot cross the 180th meridian, so query both sides separately. A ground is found through its pins with a coordinate; the day of a ground without any coordinate appears only in the files. For every data partner and ground in the box, only its most recent visible day is returned. The pins of a day D become visible at about 07:00 local time at the ground, not when they are sent: at a small club the working hours of one greenkeeper would otherwise be readable. Local time is taken from longitude, not from time zones: visible_from is D 07:00 UTC minus round(mean lon / 15) hours, with halves rounded up. Cached for five minutes in the reader's browser, never in shared caches; the ETag lets a client ask again without the body. Live records can still change until the day closes; for anything kept, use the files.

get.description: The same key, CORS, limits and box as GET /live; the two endpoints share one day counter per GitHub account, so an account has 1000 requests a UTC day across both. from and to are required: from not after to, at most 31 days, and to must be a closed day (D + 3 days, 00:00 UTC). The answer is a GeoJSON FeatureCollection whose records are those of the day files of the range (FORMAT.md 4.2): a ground is in the box as soon as one of its rows has a coordinate in the box, and then all its rows in the range come. The title in notes names the range, and as_of is to. Cached for one day in the reader's browser, never in shared caches; a closed day does not change.

get.summary: Start the GitHub login for a reader key
get.description: Redirects (302) to GitHub, asking only for the login. A random state travels in a cookie ops_state (Path=/v1/auth, Max-Age=600) and back in the URL; the callback wants them equal. GitHub returns to /auth/github/callback.

302.description: The Location header points at github.com/login/oauth/authorize.

Set-Cookie.description: ops_state, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/v1/auth, Max-Age=600.

503.description: The live API is not configured on this server.

example.title: Service Unavailable
example.detail: the live API is not configured on this server

get.summary: GitHub returns here; the answer is the key
get.description: Checks the state against the cookie, trades the code for a token, reads the GitHub id and login name, and issues one key. The token is used and dropped, never stored. The answer is an HTML page that shows the key once; a blocked account gets an HTML page with 403 and no key.

200.description: An HTML page with the key, shown once. The ops_state cookie is dropped.

400.description: The state is missing or does not match the cookie.

example.title: Bad Request
example.detail: the login could not be verified, start again

403.description: The GitHub account is blocked and gets no key; the answer is an HTML page.

502.description: The GitHub login could not be completed.

example.title: Bad Gateway
example.detail: the GitHub login could not be completed

503.description: The live API is not configured on this server.

post.summary: Deliver the pins of one ground for one day
post.description: A submission replaces everything the same data partner sent for the same group and date; holes it does not name are gone afterwards. To correct a day, send the whole day again. The key comes first: a missing key is answered before size and JSON are looked at. The body is at most 64 KiB. All pins with a coordinate must lie within 5 km of each other: one submission is one ground. A field that is not named in API.md 1.1, in the envelope or in a pin, is a problem even when it is null. If any check fails, nothing is stored. The date must lie within one day of today's UTC date (yesterday, today or tomorrow) and the day must still be open.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: With dry_run=true (or 1) everything is checked and nothing is stored; the answer says stored 0 and dry_run true. Without dry_run, or with false or 0, the pins are stored. Any other value, an empty one too, is 400 invalid_dry_run, so a misspelt switch never stores.

400.description: The body is not JSON, or dry_run has another value than true, false, 1 or 0.

invalid_dry_run.summary: dry_run is neither true, false, 1 nor 0

value.title: Bad Request
value.detail: dry_run must be true or false

413.description: The body is larger than 64 KiB.

example.title: Content Too Large
example.detail: the body is larger than 64 KiB

422.description: The submission has problems. problems lists each problem with hole (or null for the envelope), field and message.

problems.message: is not a field of a pin

429.description: A data partner waiting for review has sent 20 grounds that day already (API.md 3.1). Replacing a ground sent that day is allowed.

example.title: Too Many Requests

delete.summary: Withdraw the pins of one ground for one day
delete.description: Withdraws everything the same data partner sent for the same group and date while the day is open. A closed day cannot be withdrawn here; a correction gets a file of its own (FORMAT.md 4.3).

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The data partner's own label for the golf ground.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The calendar date at the ground, YYYY-MM-DD.

200.description: The pins were withdrawn. deleted is the number of rows removed and is 0 when there was nothing to remove.

400.description: group or date is missing, or date is not a real calendar date.

409.description: The day is already published and cannot be withdrawn here.

get.description: The index of FORMAT.md 4.3: one entry per published file with path, kind, date or year, bytes, sha256 and rows. The index is written last and points at no file that is not there yet. Cached for five minutes. 404 while nothing has been published.

Every record with that date, from all courses and channels (FORMAT.md 4.1). The file is written once, when the day closes at D + 3 days 00:00 UTC, and does not change after that; cached for one year. 404 until it has been published.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The calendar date of the day file.

404.description: The day has not been published yet.

get.description: Every record with that date, from all courses and channels (FORMAT.md 4.2). The file is written once, when the day closes at D + 3 days 00:00 UTC, and does not change after that; cached for one year. 404 until it has been published.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The calendar date of the day file.

404.description: The day has not been published yet.

get.description: All published days of a year, in the order of FORMAT.md 2.2. The file is rebuilt as further days of the year are published, so it is not frozen like a day file; cached for five minutes. 404 while nothing of the year has been published.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year of the year file.

404.description: Nothing of the year has been published yet.

readerKey.description: The key of a reader (opr_...), from the GitHub login at GET /auth/github, shown once. Sent as Authorization: Bearer. One key per GitHub account is active and a new login replaces it; only its sha256 is stored. A key in the query string is not accepted. Limits per GitHub account: 30 requests a minute and 1000 per UTC day; a key may be bound to the origins of a website.

partnerKey.description: The key of a data partner (opp_...). A partner signs up on the account page at /v1/account after logging in with GitHub and agreeing that its pins are shared under the Open Database License 1.0; the page shows the key once. One key is active; a new key replaces the old one at once. Only its sha256 is stored.

ProblemDetails.description: An error as problem details (RFC 9457), served as application/problem+json. type is always about:blank and title the reason phrase of the status; error is the fixed code to branch on, and detail its fixed sentence.

title.description: The reason phrase of the status (RFC 9110, 15).

detail.description: The fixed sentence of the code.

problems.description: Only on 422 invalid_submission, one entry per problem.

hole.description: The hole the problem belongs to, or null for the envelope.

PinProperties.description: The columns of FORMAT.md 2 except lat and lon (FORMAT.md 4.2). Unknown values are left out, not written as null.

date_basis.description: local, or utc where the local date was not recorded and date is the UTC date.

hole.description: The hole number as the club names it (7, B3).

accuracy_m.description: Horizontal accuracy in metres: the radius that holds the true position with 95 % probability (FORMAT.md 2.3). Required for surveyed and detected, optional for mapped, absent for estimated.

front_m.description: Metres from the front edge of the green, seen from the line of play.

left_m.description: Metres from the left edge of the green, seen from the line of play.

input_front.description: What was typed: distance from the front edge, in input_unit.

input_offset.description: What was typed: distance from the side edge, in input_unit.

input_side.description: The edge input_offset is measured from.

channel.description: The channel the record came through (FORMAT.md 5).

missing.description: A pin was set that day, but its position is lost.

play_bearing_deg.description: Direction of the line of play at the green, degrees clockwise from true north, at most 1 decimal. Only with input_*; with it the conversion of input_* can be redone.

correction.description: How a surveyed position was corrected: none, ppp (precise point positioning, including Galileo HAS), rtk (real time against a base or a network) or ppk (worked out afterwards against a reference station). Only with source surveyed.

geometry.description: A Point [lon, lat], or null where the row has no coordinate (RFC 7946, 3.2). A lost position always has null.

FeatureCollection.description: An RFC 7946 FeatureCollection with the members of FORMAT.md 4.2. The answers of /live and /pins read like a published file; the first note names what the collection holds.

PinInput.description: The typed values of an estimated position. It holds input_front, input_offset, input_side and input_unit as front, offset, side and unit.

PositionPin.description: A pin with a position or with the typed values of an estimated position. An optional field that is null counts as absent.

play_bearing_deg.description: Direction of the line of play the input was converted with, degrees clockwise from true north, at most 1 decimal. Only with input; optional, but a partner that converts typed distances should send it (FORMAT.md 2.1).

correction.description: How a surveyed position was corrected. Only with source surveyed.

MissingPin.description: A lost position: a pin was set, but its position is lost.

SubmissionPin.description: A position pin or a lost position.

group.description: The data partner's own label for one golf ground. It is never published; it only tells OpenPinsheet which earlier submission a new one replaces.

date.description: The calendar date at the ground. Published as date with date_basis local.

stored.description: The number of pins stored, or 0 with dry_run.

replaced.description: True when an earlier submission of the same group and date was replaced.

visible_from.description: The moment the day becomes visible in GET /live.

dry_run.description: Present and true only with dry_run=true or dry_run=1.

submissionUnknownField.summary: Rejected: a misspelt field named accuracy instead of accuracy_m
submissionUnknownField.description: Deliberately invalid: POST /submissions answers 422 invalid_submission, with a problem for the field accuracy.

RateLimitLimit.description: The day limit of the key.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the UTC day.

RateLimitReset.description: The next 00:00 UTC, when the day limit starts again, in Unix seconds.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before the next try.

ETag.description: A strong validator of the answer; send it back in If-None-Match.

WWWAuthenticate.description: The scheme the key goes in: Bearer realm="openpinsheet".

Unauthorized.description: The key is missing, unknown or revoked; always the same answer.

example.title: Unauthorized
example.detail: a valid key is required in the header Authorization: Bearer

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path does not take this method; Allow lists the ones it takes.

example.title: Internal Server Error
example.detail: the request could not be completed

NotModified.description: If-None-Match matched the ETag of the answer: nothing changed. The request still counts against the limits.
